audit.why: 45.03% over 322 games — Ambessa's second-worst matchup in the table.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Ambessa six of seven stages on a lane she loses 45.03% of the time, and the full layer calls it 'Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10' with the level-chart caption 'Yours from level 1'. The prose says the opposite: 'Level 6 is where this lane turns on you', 'This is lost if it goes long, full stop', and whys[3] through whys[6] all describe Kassadin winning. The chart also credits Ambessa the first-item and two-item stages that late explicitly gives away.
audit.why: This is a race Ambessa loses by default. Her only owned stage is level 3, when Sundering Slam is unlocked and Riftwalk does not exist yet; levels 1-2 are even because neither champion can commit; everything from 4-5 onward belongs to a champion who scales and blinks.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Skill / Ambessa / Kassadin / Kassadin / Kassadin / Kassadin in both layers — Kassadin 4, Ambessa 1, Skill 2, which fits 45.03%. Difficulty rating raised from 4/10 to 7.5/10, the final rating line changed from 'Favoured' to 'Hard', and the chart caption corrected from 'Yours from level 1'. Phase ratings raised on the stages that flipped.

audit.whatIsWrong: Riftwalk is described five times without its cooldown, and two of Kassadin's abilities have no spike attached because they are not on the page at all.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2 seconds at 500 range for 40 mana, with extra blinks costing more mana but dealing more damage. Two seconds is the number that explains why 'you cannot stick to him' — it is not a cooldown you wait out, it is a movement mode. Nether Blade is a 7-second auto reset that adds significant bonus magic damage and restores mana, and Force Pulse is a 21-second cone slow that charges from spells cast in his vicinity.
audit.corrected: 5/3.5/2s stated in mid, whys[4], whys[6], spikes[1].text and spikes[3].text. Nether Blade and Force Pulse added to late, spikes[3].text and whys[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: The page refers to 'his Q silence' in five separate fields and builds advice on it: 'Bait his Q silence first or it cancels your ability-into-empowered-auto weave mid-cast', 'his Q silence shuts off your ability-weaving', 'his Q silence cancels your weave mid-cast', 'his Q silence cuts your ability-into-empowered-auto chain mid-cast', 'Bait his Q silence empty'. Riot's text for Null Sphere is: 'dealing damage and interrupting channels. The excess energy forms around himself, granting a temporary shield that absorbs magic damage.' It interrupts channels. Ambessa's kit carries no channel flag on any ability.
audit.why: This is a fabricated threat that the page then builds a whole behaviour around — hold your combo, bait his Q, only then weave. None of that is necessary, and following it costs an Ambessa player the one phase of the lane she can actually win. Meanwhile the genuine interaction is inverted from the page's assumption: Force Pulse 'draws energy from spells cast in his vicinity', so your own ability weaving is what charges the cone slow he uses on you. And Void Stone's unit-collision immunity means you cannot body-block him with the wave.
audit.corrected: All five silence references removed and replaced with what Null Sphere actually does. Force Pulse's charge-from-nearby-spells rule added to mid, whys[3], wants.you[2] and spikes[3].text. Void Stone's collision immunity added to early and whys[1].

audit.why: The trading plan — be greedy pre-6, land Cunning Sweep to unlock Sundering Slam, ride the Lacerate slow in — is right, and it is right for the right reason: an immobile melee-range AP with no dash until 6. Kept, with the fabricated silence-bait step removed from in front of it.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'once his blink is back up you cannot stick to him' names no number.
audit.why: Riftwalk at rank 1 is 5 seconds — that IS a punishable window, and the page throws it away by not saying so. By rank 3 it is 2 seconds and the window is gone, which is the real reason the lane has a shelf life.
audit.corrected: Both ends of the range stated in mid, spikes[1].text and breakdown.cooldowns, so the player knows the window exists early and expires.

audit.why: 'Kassadin takes reduced magic damage and ignores unit collision.' The collision half matters in a melee lane: a wave between you is not a wall to him, so plans that rely on trapping him behind minions fail.

edits.before: Pre-6 is the only part of this lane that's yours, so be greedy with it. Kassadin has no mobility until Riftwalk, and his Q shield only soaks AP — your kit is entirely physical, so it does nothing against you. At level 3 land Cunning Sweep to unlock Sundering Slam (doubled on the first body), then ride your Lacerate slow in with a Drakehound's Step dash; his only out is walking. Bait his Q silence first or it cancels your ability-into-empowered-auto weave mid-cast.
edits.after: Pre-6 is the only part of this lane that's yours, so be greedy with it. Kassadin has no mobility until Riftwalk, and Null Sphere's shield absorbs magic damage, so your entirely physical kit walks straight through it. At level 3 land Cunning Sweep to unlock Sundering Slam (doubled on the first body), then ride your Lacerate slow in with a Drakehound's Step dash. Void Stone lets him ignore unit collision, so the wave will never hold him for you.

edits.before: Level 6 is where this lane turns on you. Public Execution still guarantees the blink-behind, suppress and stun, but Riftwalk lets him simply teleport out of your re-position and out of every Lacerate dash you throw, so the lockdown stops converting to a kill. Spend your one R cleanly — ideally to all-in him the instant he wastes a Riftwalk — because once his blink is back up you cannot stick to him. Don't burn Flash chasing blinks across the lane.
edits.after: Level 6 is where this lane turns on you. Public Execution still guarantees the blink, suppress and stun, but Riftwalk is a 500-range blink on 5 seconds at rank 1 and 2 by rank 3, so he leaves every Lacerate dash behind and the lockdown stops converting. Spend your one R the instant he wastes a Riftwalk, while 5 seconds is still a real window. And watch Force Pulse: spells cast near him are what charge it, so your own weave loads his slow.

edits.before: This is lost if it goes long, full stop. Two-item Kassadin Riftwalks in, one-shots, and Riftwalks out, and his Q silence shuts off your ability-weaving the moment you commit. You deal almost purely physical damage into a target you can't pin, while his Q shield and Catalyst/RoA sustain blunt the chip you do land. Your only realistic win was closing the game off your pre-6 lead — group, take towers, and make the map matter before his Riftwalk scaling does.
edits.after: This is lost if it goes long, full stop. Two-item Kassadin Riftwalks in on a 2-second cooldown, one-shots, and Riftwalks out. Nether Blade loads his autos with bonus magic damage every 7 seconds, and Force Pulse's cone slow charges off the very spells you weave. You deal almost purely physical damage into a target you can't pin, while Catalyst and RoA sustain blunt what you land. Your only realistic win was closing off your pre-6 lead — group and take towers.

notes: The 'Q silence' error runs through five fields here and it is wholly invented — Riot's Null Sphere text reads 'dealing damage and interrupting channels', with no silence, and Ambessa's kit carries no channel on any ability, so there is nothing of hers for it to interrupt. Every Kassadin matchup in the repo should be grepped for 'silence'. The chart was also the most inverted in my slice: six of seven stages awarded to Ambessa on a 45.03% lane, with the full layer captioning it 'Yours from level 1' and rating it a favoured 4/10 — I raised the rating to 7.5/10 and changed the final-rating line to 'Hard', which are judgement calls the user may want to review, though a 45% win rate and the page's own 'this is lost if it goes long' both point the same way. Genuinely new interaction added: Force Pulse 'draws energy from spells cast in his vicinity', so Ambessa's own ability weaving is what charges the cone slow used against her — the page had this backwards, warning about a silence that does not exist while missing the one thing her playstyle actually feeds.
